query: do the health probes need a bearer token
positive: The health and readiness routes never require a credential. Nomad's check stanza sends no credential, and guarding them makes the orchestrator read a 401 as an unhealthy task and restart it forever.
negative: Every model route requires a bearer token, presented as an Authorization header with the Bearer scheme.

query: swagger ui broken when auth is on
positive: The page itself needs a read key, and once it loads the Swagger bundle fetches the spec over XHR with no Authorization header, because FastAPI generates the page with no request interceptor. So the spec never loads and Try it out cannot send a credential.
negative: Read the schema with curl instead, passing the key as an Authorization header.

query: why do a bad key and an under-privileged key look identical
positive: An unknown key and a key whose role is too low return the same status, code and message. Distinguishing them would let a caller enumerate valid keys by their error message.
negative: Both responses carry a WWW-Authenticate header naming the Bearer scheme.

query: does embark generate its own request id or reuse mine
positive: Send your own request id header and embark echoes it. embark sits behind a gateway that has already minted the id an operator will search for, and replacing it would make embark's logs uncorrelatable with the hop in front of them.
negative: Every response carries a request id header, and every log line the request writes carries the same value, so one grep ties a failed request to everything logged while serving it.

query: request id on a 500 response
positive: The 500 an unhandled exception produces carries the header too. Starlette renders that response outside every HTTP middleware, so the error renderer reads the id from a context variable rather than relying on the middleware that sets the header on every other response.
negative: Every response carries a request id header, and every log line the request writes carries the same value under request_id.

query: what does forge write into the destination besides the graph
positive: The manifest and the tokenizer are written beside the exported graph, and the export refuses if the exporter produced no graph or the source ships no fast tokenizer.
negative: Only a directory the exporter created is removed on failure. A pre-existing one is left alone.

query: why is the derivation kept free of network and torch
positive: It is pure on purpose: configs in, a manifest out, no network, no torch, no filesystem. The export is slow and needs a large download; the derivation is where the interesting mistakes live, so it is kept where a test can reach it in milliseconds.
negative: Nothing there is typed per model. Every field comes from a file the model author wrote, which is what stops the artifact and the model drifting apart.

query: the 514 vs 512 disagreement
positive: Two files declare a length and they disagree: the reranker's config says a positional capacity of 514 while its tokenizer config says a model max length of 512. The larger one passes every static check embark makes and then dies at warm-up.
negative: The tokenizer's declared value is often a sentinel standing for no limit, so it is range-checked rather than trusted.

query: each config file parsed into a typed model
positive: Each file is parsed into a Pydantic model at the point it is read, which turns a renamed or missing key into one validation error there instead of a key error somewhere downstream.
negative: The files disagree with each other on purpose and by accident. A repo may ship one config and not the other, or neither.

query: why is forge a separate package from core
positive: torch and optimum are why forge is its own package: they are a gigabyte of build-time machinery that has no business on the box running inference.
negative: optimum-onnx rather than the optimum exporters extra: optimum 2.x moved the ONNX exporter out into its own distribution.

query: why does the staging directory get a random name
positive: A temporary directory is made for a name nothing else holds, then freed for the rename: a crashed earlier run may have left a predictable name behind, and renaming onto an existing directory fails.
negative: Both paths share a parent, so the rename is within one filesystem.

query: why not quantize straight into the destination
positive: Nothing the command does can delete an existing artifact until a complete, verified replacement is ready to take its place. Quantizing straight into the destination and cleaning up on failure is what deleted a user's 295MB model once already.
negative: An existing destination is refused unless force is given, because int8 vectors do not match the FP32 vectors an existing store was built from.

query: does the reranker generalise past its 14 training languages
positive: It is trained on mMARCO, MS MARCO machine-translated into 14 languages, and it generalises beyond those.
negative: It is a multilingual MiniLMv2 cross-encoder on an XLM-RoBERTa base, and it is Apache 2.0 licensed.

query: how do I read the openapi spec with auth on
positive: Read the schema with curl, passing the key as an Authorization header, because the browser docs page cannot attach one to its own spec fetch.
negative: The page itself needs a read key, and the Swagger bundle then fetches the spec over XHR with no Authorization header.

query: case of the request id header
positive: The header name is read case-insensitively, as HTTP requires.
negative: A supplied id is truncated to 128 characters before it is used.

query: what is in the embeddings response envelope
positive: The response is OpenAI's envelope carrying object, data, model and usage, with one entry per input in the order given.
negative: It follows OpenAI's embeddings shape, so a client pointed at embark instead of OpenAI needs no code change.

query: 422 on a rerank call
positive: A body that fails schema validation is a 422 with the code invalid_request.
negative: An empty documents list is a 400 with the code invalid_input.

query: how does one broken model affect the others
positive: The process may already be serving other models, so one broken model parks itself and reports which, rather than taking the others down.
negative: If one configured model cannot be resolved, resolution fails and names it, because serving three of four is worse than not starting.

query: arena memory not given back
positive: ONNX Runtime allocates activations from an arena that grows to the peak it has seen and does not readily give memory back.
negative: Threads share the weights, which is the real advantage over a process pool, but they do not share intermediate tensors.

query: what module holds the batchers
positive: The batched embedder and batched reranker are defined in the batching module.
negative: The offload helper that hands work to the executor is defined in the runners module.

query: gemma terms pass downstream
positive: Commercial use is allowed, but the Gemma terms pass downstream to anyone you ship to.
negative: The licence is the Gemma Terms of Use rather than Apache 2.0.

query: mteb ranking under 500M params
positive: It ranks first on the MTEB multilingual, English and code leaderboards among models under 500M parameters.
negative: It covers 100+ languages and takes 2k tokens of context.

query: static quantization accuracy on a generic corpus
positive: Dynamic measured more accurate on CPU, at cosine 0.96 against 0.80 for static on a generic calibration set.
negative: A generic corpus calibrates for a distribution you do not serve, and the result is quietly wrong for your data in a way no shape check catches.

query: does quantization change the manifest
positive: The tokenizer and the manifest are copied unchanged. Quantization changes the weights, not the contract.
negative: A quantized artifact is not interchangeable with its FP32 source, so re-index or keep the two apart.

query: is any inference run at load time
positive: Loading opens no onnxruntime session and runs no inference.
negative: The runner opens a session anyway, so it checks the declared output width there, at startup.

query: provider order matters
positive: Providers come from the runtime providers setting, in order, and every one of them must be available.
negative: On the Jetson the chain starts with TensorRT and falls back through CUDA to CPU.

query: why the error renderer reads a context variable
positive: Starlette renders the 500 response outside every HTTP middleware, so the error renderer reads the id from a context variable rather than relying on the middleware that sets the header on every other response.
negative: Every response carries the request id header, and every log line carries the same value.

query: what happens when auth is enabled with no keys
positive: Enabling auth with no keys configured refuses at startup rather than accepting every caller.
negative: Auth is on by default, and disabling it is the documented way to serve without credentials locally.

query: dot product index after truncation
positive: Handing back a shorter vector without renormalizing would be invisible under cosine similarity and silently wrong under a dot-product index, which is the index you would choose because you truncated.
negative: OpenAI's own text-embedding-3 models re-normalize too, so a client switching over sees the same norms.

query: sending input_type to real openai
positive: A gateway that passes unknown fields through costs nothing, so sending the field against real OpenAI is harmless.
negative: It is not part of OpenAI's schema, and it defaults to document.
